newsitem.title: PERU: Two women jailed after paying respects to MRTA dead.
newsitem.headline: Two women jailed after paying respects to MRTA dead.

text.p: The wife and sister of jailed Marxist rebels were arrested after paying their respects to the grieving mother of a guerrilla killed in the raid on the Japanese ambassador's home, sources close to the family said on Saturday.

Peruvian police arrested the women late on Friday after they left the house of Maria Fernandez de Rojas, mother of Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement guerrilla Rolly Rojas who died along with 13 other rebels in a fiery military strike to free the hostages.

"Two women from the families of the MRTA rebels were arrested last night after they had left the house of the Rojas family," the family's source said. "They came to pay their respects to the Rojas family."

The Peruvian Association for Human Rights, APRODEH, and a source close to the Rojas family confirmed that those arrested were Rosa Cardenas, 46, whose husband is in prison, and Susana Roque, 34, whose brother is in prison.
The women were being held at the headquarters of the anti-terrorism police DINCOTE, local Radio Programas said.
The two men have been sentenced to life imprisonment at Yanamayo prison in the Andean highlands for MRTA guerrilla activity, APRODEH said.
"DINCOTE told me they were arrested because they were 'acting suspicious,'" APRODEH deputy-director Miguel Jugo said.
Army and navy commandos rescued all but one of the 72 hostages alive in last Tuesday's raid, which ended a 126-day siege at the diplomatic mansion.
